# A bracket under a `for` is its copy's, as its mounted path is the
# interpreter's: a copy whose `if` turns false ends its own lifetime and no
# other. The lowered settle matched brackets by their place in the list of
# those the position described, so one dropping out of the middle moved every
# copy after it, and each was ended and begun again -- on the Pokédex, every
# species request after one that answered asked again.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var mounts list[string] = []
var unmounts list[string] = []
var done list[string] = []

component page ui.node {
    var names = ["a", "b", "c"]

    for var n = names {
        if !done.contains(n) {
            effect(on=n, @mount(k) { mounts.push(k) }, @unmount(k) { unmounts.push(k) })
        }
    }
    ui.text(value="{mounts.length()}")
}

func testADroppedCopyLeavesTheRest(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.wait(func() => mounts.length() == 3, 5000)
    done.push("a")
    t.wait(func() => unmounts.length() > 0, 5000)
    t.wait(func() => mounts.length() > 3, 300)
    t.assert(unmounts.format(",") == "a")
    t.assert(mounts.format(",") == "a,b,c")
    done.push("c")
    t.wait(func() => unmounts.length() > 1, 5000)
    t.assert(unmounts.format(",") == "a,c")
    t.assert(mounts.format(",") == "a,b,c")
}

ui.window {
    page
}
